summary: The root أذي primarily signifies harm, hurt, or annoyance, whether physical or mental.

headwords.def: أَذَّى inf. n. of 1. (T, M, Msb, K.) [As a simple subst., A state of annoyance or molestation. ] And [ Annoyance, molestation, harm, or hurt: quasi-] inf. n. of آذَاهُ . (S, K.) It signifies also, [like and ,] كُلُّ مَا تَأْذَّيْتَ [ Anything by which thou art annoyed, molested, harmed, or hurt ]; (T;) or مَا يُؤْذِيكَ [ a thing that annoys, molests, harms, or hurts thee ]: (Mgh:) or a slight evil; less than what is termed ضَرَر . (El-Khattábee.) You say, أَمَاطَ الأَذَى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ He removed, or put away, or put at a distance, what was hurtful from the road, or way. (Mgh and TA in art. ميط .) Also A thing held to be unclean, dirty, or filthy: so in the Kur ii. 222. (Mgh, Msb.) [ Filth; impurity: often used in this sense in books on practical law.]

headwords.def: أَذٍ Experiencing, or suffering, [ annoyance, molestation, harm, hurt, or] what is disagreeable, or hateful, or evil, (M, * K, * Msb,) in a great, or vehement, degree; (M, K;) applied to a man; (M, Msb;) as also : (M, K:) and both signify the contr.; i. e. doing what is disagreeable, or hateful, or evil, in a great, or vehement, degree. (K.) Also, applied to a camel, That will not remain still in one place, by reason of a natural disposition, not from pain, (El-Umawee, A'Obeyd, S, M, K,) nor disease; (K;) as also : (M:) fem. of the former أَذِيَةٌ ; (El-Umawee &c.;) and of the latter . (TA.)
إِذَا : and إِذًا : see art. اذا .

headwords.def: آذِىٌّ , (S, M, K, &c.,) with medd and teshdeed, (TA, [in the CK, erroneously, اَذِىّ ,]) Waves (S, M, K) of the sea: (S:) or vehement waves: (TA:) or the أَطْبَاق [app. meaning rollers, because they fall over like folds,] which the wind raises from the surface of the water, less than ( دُونَ [but this sometimes signifies above ]) what are termed مَوْج : (ISh, TA:) pl. أَوَاذِىُّ . (S.)
